items.title: pinky
items.description: Let AI agents use your phone, with you in the loop.
items.summary: Pinky is a free and open-source tool that allows AI agents to operate real Android and iOS devices over the Model Context Protocol (MCP) with human oversight. It runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux, enforcing human approvals for risky actions like payments while hiding sensitive apps and fields by default. On Android, USB debugging must be turned on, and the phone must accept the computer's key or pair over Wi-Fi. For iOS, an iPhone takes taps and typing from a computer only through a helper app on the phone: WebDriverAgent, which you build and install once from Xcode with your Apple ID. The tool supports connections via USB, Wi-Fi, and Tailscale.

items.title: devvm
items.description: One VM for every project. An isolated sandbox with your project’s toolchain, ready for you or a coding agent to start coding
items.summary: Devvm creates an isolated VM sandbox for each project, equipped with the toolchain required by the project's files, allowing you or a coding agent to start coding. It runs tools like Claude Code, Codex, and opencode inside the VM, includes Docker, Nix, and desktop layers, and defaults new VMs to an 'allowlist' network tier. The coding agent runs inside the VM's shell rather than being installed on the host machine, ensuring that any attack on the agent stays within the sandbox. The VM mounts the project folder at the same path but otherwise sees nothing else in the home folder, and secrets like a Claude Code token or Codex login stay on the host while devvm's proxy inserts real credentials into outgoing requests. New VMs default to an 'allowlist' network tier, reaching only a defined set of hosts through a proxy running on the host machine. Developers can adjust this to 'internet' or 'open' tiers, or tighten it to 'none', depending on the network access needed for the sandboxed project or agent.

The tool aims to produce text that's clearer and more concise, not to produce text that fools someone into thinking a human wrote it. The skill is free, MIT-licensed, and designed to improve readability without trying to beat detection tools.

items.title: persona
items.summary: A persona non grata is a Latin phrase meaning “unwelcome person.” As a legal term, it refers to the practice of a state prohibiting a diplomat from entering the country as a diplomat, or censuring a diplomat already resident in the country for conduct unbecoming of the status of a diplomat. The term was first used in 1877. Beyond diplomatic contexts, it can refer to anyone who is not popular or accepted by others. In non-diplomatic usage, a country can declare non-diplomats persona non grata, as seen in the Philippines and Spain.

items.summary: MACaQ is a model-agnostic quantization method that can quantize and run text, image, video, and audio models using frameworks like llama.cpp, vLLM, Diffusers, and PyTorch. It can quantize a 122B-parameter model in 64 minutes using just 32.5 GB of device memory, achieving lower perplexity than MR-GPTQ and DuQuant++, or matching their best perplexity with 11× less quantization time. It supports backends such as Diffusers for image, video, and audio generation, and vLLM for text generation and serving. The method adds only 2.3% end-to-end overhead over pure FP16 on Qwen3-32B in vLLM.

items.title: headless
items.description: Agent skill that sets up a headless Mac, Linux or Windows machine over SSH, step by step, without ever seeing the admin password.
items.summary: To set up a headless SSH agent on Linux using 1Password, first, ensure the 1Password Client is installed with `sudo apt install 1password`. Then, configure 1Password by creating the directory `mkdir -p ~/.config/1Password/` and the file `~/.config/1Password/settings.json` with `{ "app.developer.sshAgent": true }`. Authorize using `op signin` and verify the SSH Agent with `ssh-add -l`. For passwordless SSH login, use `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` on Linux and macOS, or `ssh-add $env:USERPROFILE\\.ssh\\id_ed25519` on Windows 11. The sources do not provide a definitive answer for setting up a headless SSH agent on Mac or Windows without seeing the admin password.

items.title: bot-hq
items.description: A team of Hermes agents you chat with, each with its own screen on one Orgo computer. Composio apps, xAI voice and X research.
items.summary: The bot-hq project on GitHub describes a team of Hermes agents each with its own screen on one Orgo computer, featuring Composio apps, xAI voice, and X research. Each agent has its own model, sign-in, memory, browser profile, and files. The app uses MCP to communicate with Hermes, and each agent has connected apps, `x_search`, tasks, routines, the Library, and messages to other bots. The Orgo computer supports up to four screens, with the first bot using the main screen and each additional bot getting its own Orgo screen. The xAI-launched Grok Bot is a team of always-on AI agents that each have their own cloud computer and can finish multi-step jobs without supervision. Composio is a software development company that provides AI Agent Infrastructure, Application Integration Platform, Developer Tools and SDKs, Enterprise AI Governance, and other services.

items.title: mindact-agent
items.description: MindAct: Community-Driven AI Agent for Claude, Obsidian, and RAG Knowledge Graphs
items.summary: MindAct is a community-driven AI agent designed to integrate with Obsidian and RAG Knowledge Graphs. It provides Obsidian-native integration, allowing it to read, link, and enrich notes directly within the Obsidian vault without any exporting or reformatting. MindAct leverages Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to pull relevant passages from users' notes, ensuring responses are grounded in personal context. It also allows users to build and query their personal knowledge graph automatically as they add notes, facilitating exploration through natural-language queries. The agent is shaped by community feedback, with feature requests and bug reports directly influencing its development.

items.title: catalyst
items.description: Cross-platform setup agent and logstash for streamlined desktop event processing
items.summary: To set up a cross-platform agent for streamlined desktop event processing, Logstash is required as an intermediary to receive events from Winlogbeat and forward them to the Bindplane agent via syslog. Winlogbeat does not have native syslog output capability. To install Logstash, use the provided commands for Linux (Debian/Ubuntu and RHEL/CentOS) and Windows. For Windows, navigate to the Logstash directory and run `logstash.bat -f C:\\logstash\\config\\winlogbeat-to-syslog.conf`. For production use, install Logstash as a Windows service using NSSM or similar tools. To install Winlogbeat on Windows systems, download and install it using the MSI installer or ZIP file, then navigate to the Winlogbeat directory and run the installation script. The sources do not provide specific details on configuring Logstash for use with the Elastic Agent or alternatives to Logstash.

items.title: numbrone
items.description: A chief of staff for your coding agents: route requests to per-project manager agents that run parallel workers in git worktrees, on herdr.
items.summary: The sources describe a setup where coding agents run in parallel using git worktrees, each with its own isolated working directory checked out from the same repository. This setup allows multiple agents to work on the same codebase without interfering with each other. Each agent's environment holds only the service it changed, and requests are routed to the appropriate agent's worktree. To avoid conflicts, it's important to use different branches for each agent and to serialize merges back to the main branch. The sources do not provide specific details about a chief of staff or her role in routing requests to per-project manager agents.

items.title: mate
items.description: Mate, your mate while you shop. A text-first shopping agent for cashback, personal discount codes, package tracking and price-drop alerts. Includes a starter agent, web chat, original icon set and docs. mate.fm
items.summary: mate (mate.fm) is an AI shopping agent that people text on iMessage or WhatsApp. It negotiates guaranteed cashback and discounts at 200,000+ US stores, handles checkout for users, and tracks packages, all for free. It can also automatically send cashback on every purchase, and users can ask for package tracking by text. mate is built by the team behind Checkmate and backed by GV and DST Global. Users have 1 hour from checkout to cancel their order and receive a full refund. Discount codes can be applied within this window, but they cannot be stacked.

items.summary: SkyDot is described as a self-hosted personal AI assistant and team workbench, ranking second in the list of top AI agent open-source projects in 2026. It emphasizes local control and avoiding vendor lock-in, with a focus on self-hosting and open-source principles. The Instagram post highlights SkyDot's capabilities in managing tasks and integrating with various tools, while also stressing its self-hosted nature to keep data local. The blog post on Vellum AI underscores the benefits of self-hosting for control, cost, and security, aligning with SkyDot's positioning as a viable open-source option.

items.summary: Linger is an open-source personal agent that runs fully on your PC, aiming to break Big Tech’s grip on AI by providing powerful local AI through efficient model–harness co-design.
